1	# Idea Brief: Goal Accessibility Preservation Training: Architectural Interventions Against Turn-Position Attention Decay in Multi-Turn LLMs
2	
3	
4	- **Idea ID**: `idea_012`
5	- **Created**: 2026-05-18
6	- **Approved**: 2026-05-18
7	- **Source**: foreign:be-idea-gen-0514-5
8	- **Level**: top-tier
9	- **Target Venues**: ARR October 2026 (submission deadline October 12, 2026) → NAACL 2027 — PRIMARY safe target with 21 weeks for experiments + paper writing, AAAI 2027 (abstracts July 21, full papers July 28, 2026, Montréal, Feb 16-23, 2027) — STRETCH goal, contingent on Phase 1+2 completing within 6 weeks from start, ARR August 2026 (submission deadline August 3, 2026) → EACL 2027 commitment (October 11, 2026) — STRETCH goal, same contingency as AAAI, NOTE: Starting May 17, AAAI (10 weeks) and ARR August (11 weeks) leave 0-3 weeks for paper writing after 8-10 week experiments. Feasible only if Phase 0-2 complete ahead of schedule. ARR October provides comfortable margin.
10	
11	## Seed Topic
12	
13	Target: EMNLP 2026, ARR submission. Track: Dialogue and Interactive Systems / Machine Learning for NLP.
14	
15	Direction: Training-time architectural fix for multi-turn position bias ("Lost-in-Middle-Turns").
16	LLMs exhibit a U-shaped attention bias across conversation turns — attending to first and last
17	turns while systematically ignoring middle turns — causing a 39% average accuracy drop in
18	multi-turn settings (validated across 15+ models, 200K+ conversations, ICLR 2026 Outstanding
19	Paper). A March 2026 theory paper proves this bias is an inherent geometric property of causal
20	transformers with residual connections (Cesaro matrix structure), present at initialization
21	before any training occurs. The only existing training-based fix (RLAAR: curriculum RL with
22	abstention rewards) recovers limited performance (62.6% → 75.1%) by teaching models to
23	abstain, but does NOT address the architectural root cause. No method exists that directly
24	targets the geometric origin of the bias with a training-time intervention.
25	
26	Seed Papers:
27	- "LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation" (ICLR 2026 Outstanding Paper, arXiv:2505.06120)
28	  — establishes the 39% drop across 6 generation tasks, 15 models, 200K conversations
29	- "Lost in the Middle at Birth" (arXiv:2603.10123) — proves U-shape is a geometric property
30	  of causal attention with residual connections (iterated Cesaro matrices), validated on
31	  untrained 24-layer Qwen2
32	- "Found in the Middle" (ACL Findings 2024, arXiv:2406.16008) — inference-time calibration
33	  subtracting positional bias from attention weights, recovers only ~15pp
34	- RLAAR (arXiv:2510.18731) — curriculum RL + abstention rewards, partial behavioral fix
35	- "When Attention Closes" (arXiv:2605.12922, May 2026) — latest mechanistic analysis via
36	  "Goal Accessibility Ratio", diagnostic only, no training fix proposed
37	
38	Known Gaps:
39	- No training-time method targets the Cesaro matrix geometric bias directly
40	- RLAAR teaches abstention (behavioral workaround), doesn't fix the attention pattern itself
41	- "Found in the Middle" is inference-time only and designed for RAG, not multi-turn generation
42	- The problem is multi-causal (verbosity, premature solutions, incorrect assumptions,
43	  over-reliance on prior turns), but position bias is the mechanistically proven root cause
44	  that enables the others
45	- Longer context windows do NOT solve this — the bias is relative (middle of whatever
46	  context is present), not absolute position dependent
47	
48	In-scope: Training-time interventions that directly address the geometric cause of
49	turn-position bias. Specifically: turn-position-aware attention regularization that penalizes
50	U-shaped attention patterns, modified positional encodings (RoPE variants) that counteract
51	the Cesaro matrix decay at turn boundaries, turn-shuffling data augmentation with
52	multi-turn consistency losses, attention entropy regularization that enforces more uniform
53	turn-level attention distribution, architectural modifications to residual connections that
54	break the geometric bias at initialization.
55	
56	NOT in-scope: Inference-time-only methods (already done by "Found in the Middle"), pure
57	prompting strategies, RAG-specific solutions, single-turn improvements, methods that only
58	teach abstention without fixing attention patterns.
59	
60	Contribution type: METHOD ONLY. Must propose a concrete training-time intervention with
61	theoretical motivation grounded in the Cesaro matrix analysis. The method must demonstrably
62	reduce the 39% multi-turn accuracy gap beyond RLAAR's recovery, AND preserve single-turn
63	performance (no regression on standard benchmarks).
64	
65	EVAL PROTOCOL:
66	TRAIN on multi-turn conversation data (use the "sharded simulation" benchmark from the
67	ICLR 2026 paper, covering 6 task types: summarization, extraction, reasoning, coding,
68	math, instruction following).
69	EVALUATE on:
70	- Multi-turn accuracy recovery (primary metric: close the 39% gap)
71	- Comparison against RLAAR baseline (must exceed its 12.5pp recovery)
72	- Comparison against "Found in the Middle" inference-time calibration
73	- Turn-position attention entropy (measure whether U-shape is reduced)
74	- Single-turn preservation (MT-Bench, MMLU — must not regress)
75	- Ablation: regularization-only vs encoding-only vs combined
76	- Analysis: visualize attention patterns before/after intervention, verify
77	  Cesaro matrix eigenvalue structure is modified
78	
79	Building blocks: Open models (Qwen2.5-7B/14B, Llama-3-8B), the ICLR 2026 paper's
80	evaluation framework and benchmark, positional encoding research (RoPE, ALiBi, NTK-aware
81	scaling), attention regularization techniques, the Cesaro matrix theoretical framework
82	for designing principled interventions.
83	
84	HARD CONSTRAINTS:
85	Compute: ≤200 H100-hours total. Fine-tune from existing checkpoints — no pretraining.
86	Attention regularization and positional encoding modifications add minimal overhead.
87	Eval: Use the established "sharded simulation" benchmark (6 tasks × 5 turn depths).
88	Must report both multi-turn recovery AND single-turn preservation.
89	
90	Look for: turn-boundary-aware RoPE modifications that reset or dampen the geometric
91	decay between turns, attention regularization losses derived directly from the Cesaro
92	matrix eigenvalue structure (targeting the specific eigenvalues that cause U-shape),
93	consistency training where the same information is placed at different turn positions
94	and the model must produce identical outputs, residual connection gating at turn
95	boundaries that prevents the accumulation pattern proven in "Lost in the Middle at Birth".
96	
97	Avoid: pure prompting tricks, inference-time-only solutions (already exists), methods
98	that only work for retrieval/RAG contexts (not multi-turn generation), approaches that
99	teach abstention instead of fixing attention (RLAAR already does this), simple data
100	augmentation without theoretical grounding, methods requiring full pretraining.
101	
102	IDEA GENERATION QUALITY CONSTRAINTS (hard rules from historical bad cases):
103	
104	1. No strawman problems: Any claim about "current methods assume X" or "current methods
105	   fail at Y" MUST cite a specific paper with a specific passage as evidence. Do NOT
106	   fabricate mainstream assumptions from pre-training knowledge. If you cannot find paper
107	   evidence, the claim is invalid.
108	
109	2. No observation-only ideas: "We discover that X happens" is NOT a contribution.
110	   Discovering a problem is not a contribution — solving it is. Output MUST include a
111	   complete method, not an analysis/benchmark/empirical study.
112	
113	3. No mediocre methods: Your method MUST answer:
114	   - Core Insight: What non-obvious structural property are you exploiting?
115	   - Why Not Obvious: Why isn't this the first thing anyone would try?
116	   - Information Exploited: What do you use that a naive baseline doesn't?
117	   - Mechanistic Argument: Without experiments, explain from principles why this works.
118	   If the method can be summarized in one sentence with zero counter-intuitive content → reject.
119	
120	4. No rehashing existing work: For every core technical component you propose, search with
121	   at least 3 different queries to confirm no directly related work exists. If you find
122	   1-2 papers doing similar things, you MUST explicitly state your specific differentiation.
123	
124	5. No experiment-padding disguise: An idea's value is NOT in how many experiments it can run.
125	   Self-check with:
126	   - "Remove experiments test": Delete all results, keep only method description — does it
127	     teach the reader something non-trivial?
128	   - "Baseline fear test": If a trivial baseline achieves similar results tomorrow, does
129	     this paper still have value?
130	   - "Citation test": In 5 years, will people cite the numbers or the insight?
131	   If any test fails → the idea is garbage, start over.
132	
133	6. The following method patterns are REJECTED (unless extremely strong structural justification):
134	   - "Add an X module" — Why this specific structure?
135	   - "Train on Y data" — Is data construction itself the contribution?
136	   - "Transfer Z from domain A to B" — What is the structural analogy between A and B?
137	   - "Combine P and Q" — Where is the synergy? Why isn't it just 1+1=2?
138	   - "Use more/bigger/stronger X" — Scaling is not a method contribution.
139	
140	COMPETITION WARNING: "When Attention Closes" (May 13, 2026) shows active competition
141	on the mechanistic analysis side. Differentiate by focusing on the TRAINING FIX (not
142	just diagnosis) and by connecting directly to the Cesaro matrix theory for principled
143	intervention design. Speed matters.
144	
145	Tag: direction=multi_turn_position_bias, contribution_type=method,
146	sub_direction=geometric_attention_fix, target_venues=["EMNLP 2026", "ACL 2026"].
147	
148	## Core Problem
149	
150	Multi-turn dialogue degrades LLM performance by 39% (ICLR 2026 best paper), driven by a geometric mechanism: Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR) — the normalized attention mass from response tokens to goal-defining tokens — declines 27-48% across conversation turns (arXiv:2605.12922). This decline correlates with RoPE positional distance growing monotonically across turns, making goal tokens progressively harder to attend to. The attention channel effectively 'closes' at predictable turn depths (τ_cross ≈ 19-23), after which models lose access to task-defining information through direct attention. Critically, many real-world multi-turn applications CANNOT use the concat-and-retry workaround: streaming dialogue systems must generate responses per-turn without seeing the full conversation; tool-calling agents invoke external APIs at each turn and cannot retroactively restructure the interaction; memory-augmented agents accumulate state across turns that is fundamentally sequential; and real-time interactive interfaces (customer service, tutoring, coding assistants) require incremental response generation. For these applications — which represent the majority of deployed multi-turn LLM use cases — the performance degradation has no existing fix. Training-time behavioral approaches (RLSTA, RLAAR, TurnWise) address *symptoms* (contextual inertia, premature commitment) through reward shaping or data augmentation but do not fix the underlying positional geometry. Position-bias distillation (Pos2Distill, EMNLP 2025) targets single-context document-ordering bias, not multi-turn semantic boundaries. The geometric root cause — position-encoding-driven attention decay across turn boundaries — remains unaddressed by any training-time intervention.
151	
152	## Opportunity / Why Now
153	
154	Three concurrent findings (2025-2026) create a precise intervention target: (1) 'When Attention Closes' (May 2026) provides the diagnostic — GAR decline is measurable, predictable (R² > 0.999 linear fit to window size), and architecture-specific, yet proposes NO training fix (acknowledged as explicit limitation); (2) position-bias calibration works at inference-time ('Found in the Middle', ACL 2024; 'Scaling a Single Dimension', ACL 2025) and at training-time for single-context (Pos2Distill, EMNLP 2025), proving the geometric mechanism is fixable, but training-time fixes for *multi-turn semantic boundaries* remain unexplored; (3) learnable attention priors (GOAT, Jan 2026 — FlashAttention-compatible via logit absorption) and context-aware RoPE (CARoPE, Jul 2025) demonstrate that position encoding is modifiable during training with minimal overhead. Furthermore, a principled argument exists for why architectural geometric fixes should outperform data augmentation approaches like TurnWise: data augmentation teaches the model to *compensate* for positional decay through learned attention patterns, but this compensation is specific to turn depths seen during training — at unseen depths, the geometric decay reasserts itself. An architectural fix (modifying RoPE distances) prevents the decay from occurring in the first place, predicting superior out-of-distribution generalization to turn depths beyond training coverage. The opportunity: bridge the diagnostic-to-intervention gap with interventions that fix geometry rather than behavior, enabling the concat-impossible applications that represent the frontier of multi-turn LLM deployment.
155	
156	## Landscape (SOTA & Limitations)
157	
158	**Behavioral training-time approaches (competitors, NOT our category):** RLSTA (arXiv:2603.04783, March 2026): RL with single-turn anchors as GRPO rewards; +22-34% on multi-turn math/code with ~500 filtered examples; requires verification signals, tested only on structured tasks. RLAAR (arXiv:2510.18731, Oct 2025): Curriculum RL with abstention rewards; 62.6%→75.1% on LiC benchmarks; teaches when to abstain rather than preventing information loss. TurnWise (arXiv:2603.16759, March 2026): Uniform random multi-turn data augmentation; 12% improvement with 10K samples; no testing of out-of-distribution turn depth generalization reported, and no analysis of whether gains persist at turn depths beyond training coverage. Key limitation shared by all behavioral approaches: they teach the model to compensate for positional decay through learned patterns, but this compensation is distribution-specific — at unseen turn depths, the underlying geometric decay reasserts. Mitigating Conversational Inertia (Feb 2026): Context Preference DPO for agent settings; reduces diagonal attention bias 10%. **Position-bias training-time approaches (adjacent but single-context):** Pos2Distill (EMNLP 2025, arXiv:2508.15709): Inter-position KL distillation transferring capabilities from advantaged to disadvantaged positions; R1 for retrieval, R2 for reasoning. Targets single-context document-ordering bias (lost-in-the-middle). Key difference from our work: operates on arbitrary document positions within a single context, not on semantic turn boundaries where positional distance grows monotonically and goal tokens are structurally defined by conversation roles. IN2/FILM-7B (ICLR 2025): Position-diverse synthetic QA for long single-context. **Inference-time approaches:** Concat-and-retry (ICLR 2026): Restructures multi-turn into single prompt; recovers ~95% of single-turn performance but CANNOT apply to streaming dialogue, per-turn tool calling, memory-augmented agents, or real-time interactive interfaces. Found in the Middle (ACL 2024): Calibrates positional attention bias by subtracting dummy-document prior; +15pp on RAG. T2PAM/ROSA (arXiv:2509.23166): Test-time parameter adaptation. **Architectural/geometric approaches (OUR category — sparse):** Scaling a Single Dimension (ACL Findings 2025): Identifies causal attention mask creates position-specific hidden states; scales one dimension for +15.2%; single-context only. GOAT (arXiv:2601.15380, Jan 2026): Learnable attention priors replacing uniform prior via Entropic Optimal Transport; -1.55 perplexity; FlashAttention-compatible by absorbing log-prior into dot-product logits; general mechanism, not multi-turn targeted. CARoPE (arXiv:2507.23083, Jul 2025): Context-aware RoPE with input-dependent frequency patterns; demonstrates trainable RoPE modification is viable with improved perplexity. Scale-Invariant Attention (May 2025): Position-dependent logit transformation for length generalization. Gated Attention (arXiv:2505.06708, NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper): Head-specific sigmoid gate after SDPA; query-dependent, always-on gating that caps influence on the residual stream; eliminates attention-sink artifacts and improves training stability; <2% latency overhead. General-purpose mechanism — not multi-turn targeted, no turn-boundary or positional awareness. Our RGG ablation component is a targeted variant with turn-depth embedding. **Theoretical frameworks:** 'When Attention Closes' (arXiv:2605.12922, May 2026): Diagnostic framework defining GAR and channel-transition; identifies failure modes across architectures. 'Lost in the Middle at Birth' (arXiv:2603.10123, March 2026): Independent theoretical framework modeling causal attention as iterated Cesàro matrix powers; derives U-shaped position bias as inherent geometric property of causal decoders with residual connections. These are independent theoretical perspectives — we empirically test in Phase 0 whether the Cesàro-predicted primacy/recency structure interacts with GAR-measured multi-turn decline, bridging these frameworks for the first time. **The gap:** No work applies training-time architectural interventions specifically to the diagnosed multi-turn GAR decline mechanism with semantic turn boundaries. Pos2Distill addresses position bias in single-context; GOAT/CARoPE/Gated Attention provide trainable position/attention mechanisms but not targeted at multi-turn; behavioral approaches treat symptoms without fixing geometry. Multi-turn geometric fixes remain unexplored.
159	
160	## Proposed Approach
161	
162	**Phase 0 — GAR Diagnostic Replication, QKA Proxy Validation & Intervention Targeting (~1.5 weeks):** Replicate the GAR measurement protocol from 'When Attention Closes' on Qwen3-8B using the ICLR 2026 sharded simulation benchmark (6 tasks × 3 representative turn depths: 5, 15, 25). Measure: (a) per-layer, per-head GAR decline curves, (b) τ_cross — the critical turn where attention channel effectively closes, (c) layer stratification — which layers lose goal access first vs. which maintain it. **QKA Proxy Validation (CRITICAL):** For the same model and tasks, compute both exact GAR (materialized attention matrix) and QKA cosine similarity (cos_sim between goal-token K vectors and response-token Q vectors at each layer) across all turn depths. Report Pearson and Spearman correlation between QKA and GAR per layer. Acceptance criterion: ρ > 0.8 at goal-critical layers. If correlation is insufficient, consider alternative proxies: (i) unnormalized Q·K dot product mean, (ii) top-k Q-K alignment (max over goal tokens rather than mean), (iii) projected Q-K alignment in RoPE-rotated space. This validation is essential — optimizing a proxy that diverges from true GAR would produce models that appear to preserve goal accessibility by the proxy metric while actually losing it. **Cesàro Bridge Test:** Measure whether the Cesàro-predicted primacy bias structure (from 'Lost in the Middle at Birth', arXiv:2603.10123) correlates with GAR decline patterns across layers — this is an empirical test bridging two independent theoretical frameworks, not an assumed connection. Key output: identification of 'goal-critical layers' (top-k layers where GAR decline correlates most with behavioral failure) + validated QKA proxy. ~20 H100-hours (inference-only, attention extraction with FlashAttention disabled for diagnostic passes).
163	
164	**Phase 1 — Turn-Boundary RoPE Compression (TB-RoPE) (~3 weeks):** Modify RoPE computation at turn boundaries to resist monotonic positional decay. Introduce a learnable per-layer compression factor γ_l ∈ (0,1] applied to inter-turn positional distances. For tokens at position p in turn t, the effective RoPE position becomes: p_eff = p_intra + γ_l · Σ_{k<t} len(turn_k), where p_intra is position within the current turn. When γ_l < 1, goal tokens in early turns appear 'closer' in positional space, directly counteracting the distance-driven GAR decline. γ_l is learned per-layer during fine-tuning (initialized at 1.0 = standard RoPE, learning rate 10× lower than main LR to prevent degenerate γ→0 solutions). Architecturally minimal: same parameter count per layer as one scalar bias, fully FlashAttention-compatible (modifies position indices before RoPE application, not the attention kernel itself), zero inference overhead beyond one multiplication per layer. **Principled advantage over data augmentation:** TB-RoPE prevents positional decay at the geometric level, meaning the model doesn't need to learn compensatory attention patterns — the decay simply doesn't occur. This predicts superior out-of-distribution generalization: a model trained on conversations of 5-15 turns should maintain goal accessibility at 20-30 turns, because the geometric fix applies uniformly regardless of turn depth. In contrast, behavioral augmentation (TurnWise) teaches compensation patterns specific to trained turn depths, which may not transfer. We test this prediction explicitly in Phase 4. Trained with LoRA (rank 64) on Qwen3-8B using WildChat/LMSYS-Chat multi-turn conversations (50K sampled) with standard next-token prediction loss + Phase 2 proxy loss. ~80 H100-hours.
165	
166	**Phase 2 — Query-Key Alignment Preservation Loss (QKA Loss) (~concurrent with Phase 1):** Using the validated proxy from Phase 0: maximize the mean dot-product similarity between goal-token key vectors and response-token query vectors at goal-critical layers. Formally: L_QKA = λ · Σ_{l∈L_crit} max(0, τ_l - sim(Q_response^l, K_goal^l))², where sim() is the proxy metric validated in Phase 0 (cosine similarity if ρ > 0.8, or the best-correlated alternative), τ_l is the minimum acceptable alignment at layer l (set at 70% of turn-1 alignment, derived from Phase 0). This requires only extracting Q and K vectors at specific token positions — fully compatible with FlashAttention since no attention weight materialization is needed. Validated by periodic exact GAR audits (every 100 training steps, one forward pass with FlashAttention disabled, ~3% wall-clock overhead, used only for logging, not gradient computation). If QKA-GAR divergence exceeds 15% during training, trigger early stopping and proxy recalibration. Computational overhead of QKA loss: ~5-8%. λ warm-up from 0 to 0.1 over first 1000 steps.
167	
168	**Phase 3 — Residual Goal Gate (RGG) — Ablation Component (~1.5 weeks):** At turn-boundary positions, insert a lightweight gating mechanism: h_out = h_in + σ(W_gate · [h_in; turn_depth_emb]) ⊙ FFN(h_in), where turn_depth_emb is a learned embedding of the current turn index (1-30). This amplifies goal-relevant signal in the residual stream at turn boundaries, providing a secondary channel for goal preservation. Parameters per layer: 2d² + 30d (negligible for d=4096). **Differentiation from Gated Attention (arXiv:2505.06708, NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper):** Qwen's gated attention applies a general-purpose, always-on sigmoid gate after SDPA to introduce non-linearity and sparsity across all tokens. RGG is fundamentally different in three ways: (i) it activates only at turn-boundary positions, not all tokens; (ii) it conditions on turn depth (via turn_depth_emb), making it explicitly position-aware in the multi-turn structure; (iii) it targets the residual stream at turn boundaries specifically to preserve goal-relevant information, rather than providing general sparsification. RGG can be understood as a turn-boundary-specialized instantiation of the broader gating principle that Qwen's work validates as effective. ~40 H100-hours.
169	
170	**Phase 4 — Evaluation (~1.5 weeks):** Primary evaluation: (a) Sharded simulation benchmark from ICLR 2026 (6 tasks × 5 turn depths) measuring performance vs. turn depth; (b) Periodic GAR audit confirming attention channel remains open post-training; (c) **Concat-and-retry as inference-time upper bound** — reporting what % of the concat-achievable performance GAPT recovers while preserving the multi-turn interface; (d) **Concat-impossible scenarios** — evaluation on streaming dialogue (per-turn response generation), multi-turn tool-calling (ToolBench multi-step), and memory-augmented conversation tasks where concat structurally cannot apply, demonstrating GAPT enables capabilities beyond concat's reach; (e) Single-turn preservation on MT-Bench and MMLU; (f) Comparison against RLSTA, RLAAR, TurnWise, and Pos2Distill (adapted to multi-turn) as baselines; (g) **TurnWise-50K baseline (CRITICAL)**: scale TurnWise-style uniform augmentation to 50K samples (matching GAPT's data scale) to isolate geometric targeting from data scaling effects. Ablations: (i) TB-RoPE alone vs. TB-RoPE + QKA loss vs. full system (+RGG); (ii) learned γ_l vs. fixed compression schedules (0.5, 0.7, 0.9); (iii) QKA threshold sensitivity (50%, 70%, 90% of turn-1 alignment); (iv) **Out-of-distribution turn depth generalization (CRITICAL)**: train on conversations with 5-15 turns, evaluate on 20-30 turns — if the geometric fix hypothesis is correct, GAPT should maintain performance at unseen depths while TurnWise-50K should degrade, providing the key mechanistic distinction; (v) QKA-GAR correlation tracking across training. ~50 H100-hours.
171

# Idea Brief: Goal Accessibility Preservation Training: Architectural Interventions Against Turn-Position Attention Decay in Multi-Turn LLMs


- **Idea ID**: `idea_012`
- **Created**: 2026-05-18
- **Approved**: 2026-05-18
- **Source**: foreign:be-idea-gen-0514-5
- **Level**: top-tier
- **Target Venues**: ARR October 2026 (submission deadline October 12, 2026) → NAACL 2027 — PRIMARY safe target with 21 weeks for experiments + paper writing, AAAI 2027 (abstracts July 21, full papers July 28, 2026, Montréal, Feb 16-23, 2027) — STRETCH goal, contingent on Phase 1+2 completing within 6 weeks from start, ARR August 2026 (submission deadline August 3, 2026) → EACL 2027 commitment (October 11, 2026) — STRETCH goal, same contingency as AAAI, NOTE: Starting May 17, AAAI (10 weeks) and ARR August (11 weeks) leave 0-3 weeks for paper writing after 8-10 week experiments. Feasible only if Phase 0-2 complete ahead of schedule. ARR October provides comfortable margin.

## Seed Topic

Target: EMNLP 2026, ARR submission. Track: Dialogue and Interactive Systems / Machine Learning for NLP.

Direction: Training-time architectural fix for multi-turn position bias ("Lost-in-Middle-Turns").
LLMs exhibit a U-shaped attention bias across conversation turns — attending to first and last
turns while systematically ignoring middle turns — causing a 39% average accuracy drop in
multi-turn settings (validated across 15+ models, 200K+ conversations, ICLR 2026 Outstanding
Paper). A March 2026 theory paper proves this bias is an inherent geometric property of causal
transformers with residual connections (Cesaro matrix structure), present at initialization
before any training occurs. The only existing training-based fix (RLAAR: curriculum RL with
abstention rewards) recovers limited performance (62.6% → 75.1%) by teaching models to
abstain, but does NOT address the architectural root cause. No method exists that directly
targets the geometric origin of the bias with a training-time intervention.

Seed Papers:
- "LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation" (ICLR 2026 Outstanding Paper, arXiv:2505.06120)
  — establishes the 39% drop across 6 generation tasks, 15 models, 200K conversations
- "Lost in the Middle at Birth" (arXiv:2603.10123) — proves U-shape is a geometric property
  of causal attention with residual connections (iterated Cesaro matrices), validated on
  untrained 24-layer Qwen2
- "Found in the Middle" (ACL Findings 2024, arXiv:2406.16008) — inference-time calibration
  subtracting positional bias from attention weights, recovers only ~15pp
- RLAAR (arXiv:2510.18731) — curriculum RL + abstention rewards, partial behavioral fix
- "When Attention Closes" (arXiv:2605.12922, May 2026) — latest mechanistic analysis via
  "Goal Accessibility Ratio", diagnostic only, no training fix proposed

Known Gaps:
- No training-time method targets the Cesaro matrix geometric bias directly
- RLAAR teaches abstention (behavioral workaround), doesn't fix the attention pattern itself
- "Found in the Middle" is inference-time only and designed for RAG, not multi-turn generation
- The problem is multi-causal (verbosity, premature solutions, incorrect assumptions,
  over-reliance on prior turns), but position bias is the mechanistically proven root cause
  that enables the others
- Longer context windows do NOT solve this — the bias is relative (middle of whatever
  context is present), not absolute position dependent

In-scope: Training-time interventions that directly address the geometric cause of
turn-position bias. Specifically: turn-position-aware attention regularization that penalizes
U-shaped attention patterns, modified positional encodings (RoPE variants) that counteract
the Cesaro matrix decay at turn boundaries, turn-shuffling data augmentation with
multi-turn consistency losses, attention entropy regularization that enforces more uniform
turn-level attention distribution, architectural modifications to residual connections that
break the geometric bias at initialization.

NOT in-scope: Inference-time-only methods (already done by "Found in the Middle"), pure
prompting strategies, RAG-specific solutions, single-turn improvements, methods that only
teach abstention without fixing attention patterns.

Contribution type: METHOD ONLY. Must propose a concrete training-time intervention with
theoretical motivation grounded in the Cesaro matrix analysis. The method must demonstrably
reduce the 39% multi-turn accuracy gap beyond RLAAR's recovery, AND preserve single-turn
performance (no regression on standard benchmarks).

EVAL PROTOCOL:
TRAIN on multi-turn conversation data (use the "sharded simulation" benchmark from the
ICLR 2026 paper, covering 6 task types: summarization, extraction, reasoning, coding,
math, instruction following).
EVALUATE on:
- Multi-turn accuracy recovery (primary metric: close the 39% gap)
- Comparison against RLAAR baseline (must exceed its 12.5pp recovery)
- Comparison against "Found in the Middle" inference-time calibration
- Turn-position attention entropy (measure whether U-shape is reduced)
- Single-turn preservation (MT-Bench, MMLU — must not regress)
- Ablation: regularization-only vs encoding-only vs combined
- Analysis: visualize attention patterns before/after intervention, verify
  Cesaro matrix eigenvalue structure is modified

Building blocks: Open models (Qwen2.5-7B/14B, Llama-3-8B), the ICLR 2026 paper's
evaluation framework and benchmark, positional encoding research (RoPE, ALiBi, NTK-aware
scaling), attention regularization techniques, the Cesaro matrix theoretical framework
for designing principled interventions.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
Compute: ≤200 H100-hours total. Fine-tune from existing checkpoints — no pretraining.
Attention regularization and positional encoding modifications add minimal overhead.
Eval: Use the established "sharded simulation" benchmark (6 tasks × 5 turn depths).
Must report both multi-turn recovery AND single-turn preservation.

Look for: turn-boundary-aware RoPE modifications that reset or dampen the geometric
decay between turns, attention regularization losses derived directly from the Cesaro
matrix eigenvalue structure (targeting the specific eigenvalues that cause U-shape),
consistency training where the same information is placed at different turn positions
and the model must produce identical outputs, residual connection gating at turn
boundaries that prevents the accumulation pattern proven in "Lost in the Middle at Birth".

Avoid: pure prompting tricks, inference-time-only solutions (already exists), methods
that only work for retrieval/RAG contexts (not multi-turn generation), approaches that
teach abstention instead of fixing attention (RLAAR already does this), simple data
augmentation without theoretical grounding, methods requiring full pretraining.

IDEA GENERATION QUALITY CONSTRAINTS (hard rules from historical bad cases):

1. No strawman problems: Any claim about "current methods assume X" or "current methods
   fail at Y" MUST cite a specific paper with a specific passage as evidence. Do NOT
   fabricate mainstream assumptions from pre-training knowledge. If you cannot find paper
   evidence, the claim is invalid.

2. No observation-only ideas: "We discover that X happens" is NOT a contribution.

   - Core Insight: What non-obvious structural property are you exploiting?
   - Why Not Obvious: Why isn't this the first thing anyone would try?

   - "Baseline fear test": If a trivial baseline achieves similar results tomorrow, does

   - "Citation test": In 5 years, will people cite the numbers or the insight?

## Core Problem

Multi-turn dialogue degrades LLM performance by 39% (ICLR 2026 best paper), driven by a geometric mechanism: Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR) — the normalized attention mass from response tokens to goal-defining tokens — declines 27-48% across conversation turns (arXiv:2605.12922). This decline correlates with RoPE positional distance growing monotonically across turns, making goal tokens progressively harder to attend to. The attention channel effectively 'closes' at predictable turn depths (τ_cross ≈ 19-23), after which models lose access to task-defining information through direct attention. Critically, many real-world multi-turn applications CANNOT use the concat-and-retry workaround: streaming dialogue systems must generate responses per-turn without seeing the full conversation; tool-calling agents invoke external APIs at each turn and cannot retroactively restructure the interaction; memory-augmented agents accumulate state across turns that is fundamentally sequential; and real-time interactive interfaces (customer service, tutoring, coding assistants) require incremental response generation. For these applications — which represent the majority of deployed multi-turn LLM use cases — the performance degradation has no existing fix. Training-time behavioral approaches (RLSTA, RLAAR, TurnWise) address *symptoms* (contextual inertia, premature commitment) through reward shaping or data augmentation but do not fix the underlying positional geometry. Position-bias distillation (Pos2Distill, EMNLP 2025) targets single-context document-ordering bias, not multi-turn semantic boundaries. The geometric root cause — position-encoding-driven attention decay across turn boundaries — remains unaddressed by any training-time intervention.

## Opportunity / Why Now

Three concurrent findings (2025-2026) create a precise intervention target: (1) 'When Attention Closes' (May 2026) provides the diagnostic — GAR decline is measurable, predictable (R² > 0.999 linear fit to window size), and architecture-specific, yet proposes NO training fix (acknowledged as explicit limitation); (2) position-bias calibration works at inference-time ('Found in the Middle', ACL 2024; 'Scaling a Single Dimension', ACL 2025) and at training-time for single-context (Pos2Distill, EMNLP 2025), proving the geometric mechanism is fixable, but training-time fixes for *multi-turn semantic boundaries* remain unexplored; (3) learnable attention priors (GOAT, Jan 2026 — FlashAttention-compatible via logit absorption) and context-aware RoPE (CARoPE, Jul 2025) demonstrate that position encoding is modifiable during training with minimal overhead. Furthermore, a principled argument exists for why architectural geometric fixes should outperform data augmentation approaches like TurnWise: data augmentation teaches the model to *compensate* for positional decay through learned attention patterns, but this compensation is specific to turn depths seen during training — at unseen depths, the geometric decay reasserts itself. An architectural fix (modifying RoPE distances) prevents the decay from occurring in the first place, predicting superior out-of-distribution generalization to turn depths beyond training coverage. The opportunity: bridge the diagnostic-to-intervention gap with interventions that fix geometry rather than behavior, enabling the concat-impossible applications that represent the frontier of multi-turn LLM deployment.

## Proposed Approach

**Phase 0 — GAR Diagnostic Replication, QKA Proxy Validation & Intervention Targeting (~1.5 weeks):** Replicate the GAR measurement protocol from 'When Attention Closes' on Qwen3-8B using the ICLR 2026 sharded simulation benchmark (6 tasks × 3 representative turn depths: 5, 15, 25). Measure: (a) per-layer, per-head GAR decline curves, (b) τ_cross — the critical turn where attention channel effectively closes, (c) layer stratification — which layers lose goal access first vs. which maintain it. **QKA Proxy Validation (CRITICAL):** For the same model and tasks, compute both exact GAR (materialized attention matrix) and QKA cosine similarity (cos_sim between goal-token K vectors and response-token Q vectors at each layer) across all turn depths. Report Pearson and Spearman correlation between QKA and GAR per layer. Acceptance criterion: ρ > 0.8 at goal-critical layers. If correlation is insufficient, consider alternative proxies: (i) unnormalized Q·K dot product mean, (ii) top-k Q-K alignment (max over goal tokens rather than mean), (iii) projected Q-K alignment in RoPE-rotated space. This validation is essential — optimizing a proxy that diverges from true GAR would produce models that appear to preserve goal accessibility by the proxy metric while actually losing it. **Cesàro Bridge Test:** Measure whether the Cesàro-predicted primacy bias structure (from 'Lost in the Middle at Birth', arXiv:2603.10123) correlates with GAR decline patterns across layers — this is an empirical test bridging two independent theoretical frameworks, not an assumed connection. Key output: identification of 'goal-critical layers' (top-k layers where GAR decline correlates most with behavioral failure) + validated QKA proxy. ~20 H100-hours (inference-only, attention extraction with FlashAttention disabled for diagnostic passes).

**Phase 1 — Turn-Boundary RoPE Compression (TB-RoPE) (~3 weeks):** Modify RoPE computation at turn boundaries to resist monotonic positional decay. Introduce a learnable per-layer compression factor γ_l ∈ (0,1] applied to inter-turn positional distances. For tokens at position p in turn t, the effective RoPE position becomes: p_eff = p_intra + γ_l · Σ_{k<t} len(turn_k), where p_intra is position within the current turn. When γ_l < 1, goal tokens in early turns appear 'closer' in positional space, directly counteracting the distance-driven GAR decline. γ_l is learned per-layer during fine-tuning (initialized at 1.0 = standard RoPE, learning rate 10× lower than main LR to prevent degenerate γ→0 solutions). Architecturally minimal: same parameter count per layer as one scalar bias, fully FlashAttention-compatible (modifies position indices before RoPE application, not the attention kernel itself), zero inference overhead beyond one multiplication per layer. **Principled advantage over data augmentation:** TB-RoPE prevents positional decay at the geometric level, meaning the model doesn't need to learn compensatory attention patterns — the decay simply doesn't occur. This predicts superior out-of-distribution generalization: a model trained on conversations of 5-15 turns should maintain goal accessibility at 20-30 turns, because the geometric fix applies uniformly regardless of turn depth. In contrast, behavioral augmentation (TurnWise) teaches compensation patterns specific to trained turn depths, which may not transfer. We test this prediction explicitly in Phase 4. Trained with LoRA (rank 64) on Qwen3-8B using WildChat/LMSYS-Chat multi-turn conversations (50K sampled) with standard next-token prediction loss + Phase 2 proxy loss. ~80 H100-hours.

**Phase 2 — Query-Key Alignment Preservation Loss (QKA Loss) (~concurrent with Phase 1):** Using the validated proxy from Phase 0: maximize the mean dot-product similarity between goal-token key vectors and response-token query vectors at goal-critical layers. Formally: L_QKA = λ · Σ_{l∈L_crit} max(0, τ_l - sim(Q_response^l, K_goal^l))², where sim() is the proxy metric validated in Phase 0 (cosine similarity if ρ > 0.8, or the best-correlated alternative), τ_l is the minimum acceptable alignment at layer l (set at 70% of turn-1 alignment, derived from Phase 0). This requires only extracting Q and K vectors at specific token positions — fully compatible with FlashAttention since no attention weight materialization is needed. Validated by periodic exact GAR audits (every 100 training steps, one forward pass with FlashAttention disabled, ~3% wall-clock overhead, used only for logging, not gradient computation). If QKA-GAR divergence exceeds 15% during training, trigger early stopping and proxy recalibration. Computational overhead of QKA loss: ~5-8%. λ warm-up from 0 to 0.1 over first 1000 steps.

**Phase 3 — Residual Goal Gate (RGG) — Ablation Component (~1.5 weeks):** At turn-boundary positions, insert a lightweight gating mechanism: h_out = h_in + σ(W_gate · [h_in; turn_depth_emb]) ⊙ FFN(h_in), where turn_depth_emb is a learned embedding of the current turn index (1-30). This amplifies goal-relevant signal in the residual stream at turn boundaries, providing a secondary channel for goal preservation. Parameters per layer: 2d² + 30d (negligible for d=4096). **Differentiation from Gated Attention (arXiv:2505.06708, NeurIPS 2025 Best Paper):** Qwen's gated attention applies a general-purpose, always-on sigmoid gate after SDPA to introduce non-linearity and sparsity across all tokens. RGG is fundamentally different in three ways: (i) it activates only at turn-boundary positions, not all tokens; (ii) it conditions on turn depth (via turn_depth_emb), making it explicitly position-aware in the multi-turn structure; (iii) it targets the residual stream at turn boundaries specifically to preserve goal-relevant information, rather than providing general sparsification. RGG can be understood as a turn-boundary-specialized instantiation of the broader gating principle that Qwen's work validates as effective. ~40 H100-hours.

**Phase 4 — Evaluation (~1.5 weeks):** Primary evaluation: (a) Sharded simulation benchmark from ICLR 2026 (6 tasks × 5 turn depths) measuring performance vs. turn depth; (b) Periodic GAR audit confirming attention channel remains open post-training; (c) **Concat-and-retry as inference-time upper bound** — reporting what % of the concat-achievable performance GAPT recovers while preserving the multi-turn interface; (d) **Concat-impossible scenarios** — evaluation on streaming dialogue (per-turn response generation), multi-turn tool-calling (ToolBench multi-step), and memory-augmented conversation tasks where concat structurally cannot apply, demonstrating GAPT enables capabilities beyond concat's reach; (e) Single-turn preservation on MT-Bench and MMLU; (f) Comparison against RLSTA, RLAAR, TurnWise, and Pos2Distill (adapted to multi-turn) as baselines; (g) **TurnWise-50K baseline (CRITICAL)**: scale TurnWise-style uniform augmentation to 50K samples (matching GAPT's data scale) to isolate geometric targeting from data scaling effects. Ablations: (i) TB-RoPE alone vs. TB-RoPE + QKA loss vs. full system (+RGG); (ii) learned γ_l vs. fixed compression schedules (0.5, 0.7, 0.9); (iii) QKA threshold sensitivity (50%, 70%, 90% of turn-1 alignment); (iv) **Out-of-distribution turn depth generalization (CRITICAL)**: train on conversations with 5-15 turns, evaluate on 20-30 turns — if the geometric fix hypothesis is correct, GAPT should maintain performance at unseen depths while TurnWise-50K should degrade, providing the key mechanistic distinction; (v) QKA-GAR correlation tracking across training. ~50 H100-hours.

---

### MVP-A: GAR 诊断复现 + QKA 代理验证

**[severity: info]** GAR decline > 20% 阈值合理。原始文献报告 27-48% GAR 衰减（arXiv:2605.12922），39% 准确率下降（ICLR 2026）。20% 是保守下限，复现失败才真正说明问题不存在。通过。

**[severity: warning]** QKA-GAR ρ > 0.8 gate 缺少 fallback 路径。IDEA_BRIEF 明确列出了 3 种备选代理指标（unnormalized Q·K dot product、top-k Q-K alignment、projected Q-K in RoPE-rotated space），但 ROADMAP 的 fail action 直接写"项目终止或 pivot"，未包含测试备选代理的步骤。建议：MVP-A 的 fail action 应先测试全部 4 种代理指标，**全部 ρ < 0.8 才触发 kill**。否则可能因代理选择不当而误杀有效项目。

---

### MVP-B: TB-RoPE 概念验证

**[severity: warning]** "单轮不退化"标准缺少量化阈值。当前写法是"单轮不退化"，但未定义容忍范围。建议明确：MT-Bench / MMLU 相对 baseline 退化 < 2pp 即 pass，> 5pp 即 fail，2-5pp 需 Director 决策。无量化标准的 gate check 在执行时会产生争议。

**[severity: warning]** Fail action "尝试其他 γ 值或 pivot" 无上界。固定 γ 的搜索空间需要有限：建议测试 γ ∈ {0.5, 0.7, 0.9} 共 3 个值，全部 fail 才 pivot。否则 Agent 可能无限调参。

---

### 跨 MVP 问题

**[severity: info]** 模型选择需澄清：MVP-A 用 Qwen3-8B（匹配理论论文），但 IDEA_BRIEF 优化方案第 12 条将训练基座改为 Llama-3-8B。MVP-B 未指定用哪个模型。建议在 ROADMAP 中明确 MVP-B 使用 Qwen3-8B（与 MVP-A 保持一致，减少变量），全量阶段再考虑 Llama-3-8B。

**[severity: info]** GPU 未配置是当前唯一阻塞项。MVP 总预算仅 ~25 H100-hours，属于轻量级。建议 Director 优先推进 GPU 分配。

---

**总结**：MVP 设计的核心逻辑（先验证现象存在性 + 代理有效性，再验证干预可行性）是合理的，假设可证伪，kill criteria 方向正确。但有 2 个 warning 需要修复：(1) QKA gate 的 fallback 代理测试路径缺失，(2) MVP-B 单轮退化阈值未量化。建议 Director 在 Agent 开始执行前更新 ROADMAP。

# GAR (Goal Accessibility Ratio) measurement for multi-turn conversations.
# Measures how much attention the model's latest-turn queries pay to goal-defining
# tokens from the first turn, across all layers and heads.
#
# Dependencies: torch, transformers
# Input: HF causal LM + tokenizer, conversation as list of turn strings, goal token positions
# Output: per-layer per-head GAR matrices (shape [n_layers, n_heads])

import torch
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional


def _build_chat_input(
    tokenizer,
    conversation: List[str],
    max_turns: Optional[int] = None,
) -> dict:
    """Build tokenized input from a multi-turn conversation.

    Alternates user/assistant roles. If max_turns is set, truncates to that many turns.
    Returns tokenizer output dict with input_ids and attention_mask on CPU.
    """
    if max_turns is not None:
        conversation = conversation[:max_turns]

    messages = []
    for i, turn in enumerate(conversation):
        role = "user" if i % 2 == 0 else "assistant"
        messages.append({"role": role, "content": turn})

    text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False)
    inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")
    return inputs


def _locate_goal_tokens(
    tokenizer,
    full_input_ids: torch.Tensor,
    goal_text: str,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Find token positions of goal_text within full_input_ids.

    Returns a 1-D tensor of position indices.
    """
    goal_ids = tokenizer.encode(goal_text, add_special_tokens=False)
    seq = full_input_ids.squeeze(0).tolist()
    goal_len = len(goal_ids)

    for start in range(len(seq) - goal_len + 1):
        if seq[start : start + goal_len] == goal_ids:
            return torch.arange(start, start + goal_len)

    # Fallback: if exact match fails, return positions of first turn tokens
    # (conservative estimate, caller should verify)
    raise ValueError(
        f"Goal text not found in input. goal_ids={goal_ids[:10]}... "
        f"seq length={len(seq)}"
    )


def _locate_last_turn_tokens(
    tokenizer,
    full_input_ids: torch.Tensor,
    last_turn_text: str,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Find token positions of the last turn within full_input_ids.

    Searches from the end to handle repeated content correctly.
    Returns a 1-D tensor of position indices.
    """
    turn_ids = tokenizer.encode(last_turn_text, add_special_tokens=False)
    seq = full_input_ids.squeeze(0).tolist()
    turn_len = len(turn_ids)

    # Search from end
    for start in range(len(seq) - turn_len, -1, -1):
        if seq[start : start + turn_len] == turn_ids:
            return torch.arange(start, start + turn_len)

    raise ValueError(f"Last turn text not found in input. turn length={turn_len}")


def compute_gar(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    conversation: List[str],
    goal_text: str,
    device: str = "cuda",
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute Goal Accessibility Ratio for a multi-turn conversation.

    GAR = sum of attention weights from last-turn query positions to goal-token
    positions, normalized by total attention from those query positions.

    Args:
        model: HuggingFace causal LM (e.g. Qwen3-8B)
        tokenizer: corresponding tokenizer
        conversation: list of turn strings, alternating user/assistant
        goal_text: the goal-defining text from the first turn to track
        device: "cuda" or "cuda:0" etc.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray of shape [n_layers, n_heads] with GAR values in [0, 1]
    """
    inputs = _build_chat_input(tokenizer, conversation)
    input_ids = inputs["input_ids"].to(device)
    attention_mask = inputs["attention_mask"].to(device)

    goal_positions = _locate_goal_tokens(tokenizer, inputs["input_ids"], goal_text)
    last_turn_positions = _locate_last_turn_tokens(
        tokenizer, inputs["input_ids"], conversation[-1]
    )

    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model(
            input_ids=input_ids,
            attention_mask=attention_mask,
            output_attentions=True,
        )

    # outputs.attentions: tuple of (batch, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len) per layer
    n_layers = len(outputs.attentions)
    n_heads = outputs.attentions[0].shape[1]
    gar = np.zeros((n_layers, n_heads))

    for layer_idx, attn in enumerate(outputs.attentions):
        # attn shape: (1, n_heads, seq_len, seq_len)
        # [query_positions, :] selects rows for last-turn queries
        # [:, goal_positions] selects columns for goal keys
        attn_matrix = attn.squeeze(0).float()  # (n_heads, seq_len, seq_len)

        query_attn = attn_matrix[:, last_turn_positions, :]  # (n_heads, n_query, seq_len)
        goal_attn = query_attn[:, :, goal_positions]  # (n_heads, n_query, n_goal)

        # GAR = sum of attention to goal / sum of all attention from these queries
        goal_sum = goal_attn.sum(dim=(1, 2))  # (n_heads,)
        total_sum = query_attn.sum(dim=(1, 2))  # (n_heads,)

        gar[layer_idx] = (goal_sum / total_sum.clamp(min=1e-10)).cpu().numpy()

    return gar


def compute_gar_curve(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    conversation: List[str],
    goal_text: str,
    turn_depths: List[int] = None,
    device: str = "cuda",
) -> Dict[int, np.ndarray]:
    """Compute GAR at different conversation depths to measure decline.

    Args:
        model: HuggingFace causal LM
        tokenizer: corresponding tokenizer
        conversation: full conversation (must have >= max(turn_depths) turns)
        goal_text: goal-defining text to track
        turn_depths: list of turn counts to evaluate at (default [5, 15, 25])
        device: compute device

    Returns:
        dict mapping turn_depth -> GAR matrix of shape [n_layers, n_heads]
    """
    if turn_depths is None:
        turn_depths = [5, 15, 25]

    results = {}
    for depth in turn_depths:
        if depth > len(conversation):
            print(f"Warning: turn_depth={depth} exceeds conversation length={len(conversation)}, skipping")
            continue

        truncated = conversation[:depth]
        gar = compute_gar(model, tokenizer, truncated, goal_text, device=device)
        results[depth] = gar
        print(f"Turn depth {depth}: mean GAR = {gar.mean():.4f}")

    return results

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# MVP-A main entry: run GAR measurement + QKA computation on Qwen3-8B.
#
# Usage:
#   python run_mvp_a.py --model_path Qwen/Qwen3-8B --output_dir ./results
#   python run_mvp_a.py --model_path /local/Qwen3-8B --turn_depths 5 10 15 20 25 --gpu 0
#
# Dependencies: torch, transformers, numpy, scipy, matplotlib

import os
import json
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List

import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

from gar_measurement import compute_gar_curve
from qka_computation import compute_qka_curve
from analysis import (
    compute_correlation_curve,
    plot_gar_decline,
    plot_qka_gar_scatter,
    plot_gar_heatmap,
    summarize_results,
)


def generate_synthetic_conversation(n_turns: int = 30) -> tuple:
    """Generate a synthetic multi-turn conversation with a clear goal.

    The first user turn defines a goal. Subsequent turns drift to test
    whether the model retains attention to the original goal tokens.

    Returns:
        (conversation: list of strings, goal_text: str)
    """
    goal_text = "plan a weekend trip to Kyoto focusing on temples and traditional cuisine"

    conversation = [
        # Turn 0 (user): defines the goal
        f"I want to {goal_text}. Can you help me create a detailed itinerary?",
        # Turn 1 (assistant)
        "I'd be happy to help you plan a Kyoto trip. Let me start with some temple recommendations. "
        "Kinkaku-ji and Fushimi Inari are must-visits. For cuisine, try kaiseki at a traditional ryokan.",
    ]

    # Filler turns that gradually drift from the original goal
    drift_topics = [
        ("What's the weather like in Japan in spring?", "Spring in Japan typically sees temperatures between 10-20C. Cherry blossom season peaks in late March to early April."),
        ("How about transportation? Is the JR Pass worth it?", "For Kyoto specifically, a bus day pass is more useful. The JR Pass is better for inter-city travel like Tokyo-Kyoto."),
        ("I heard about some good hiking trails near Kyoto.", "The Fushimi Inari trail is popular. For more serious hiking, consider the Daimonji mountain or the Philosopher's Path area."),
        ("What about shopping areas?", "Nishiki Market is great for food souvenirs. Teramachi Street has traditional crafts. Gion has high-end shops."),
        ("Any recommendations for day trips from Kyoto?", "Nara is just 45 minutes away and has a famous deer park. Osaka is 30 minutes for street food. Uji is known for matcha."),
        ("How do I handle money in Japan? Cash vs cards?", "Japan is still quite cash-heavy. Most temples and small restaurants only accept cash. Convenience stores have international ATMs."),
        ("What are some cultural etiquette tips?", "Remove shoes when entering temples and some restaurants. Bow when greeting. Don't tip. Be quiet on public transport."),
        ("Can you recommend some Japanese phrases I should learn?", "Sumimasen (excuse me), Arigatou gozaimasu (thank you), Kore wa ikura desu ka (how much is this) are essentials."),
        ("What about accommodation options?", "Traditional ryokans offer the best cultural experience. Business hotels are budget-friendly. Capsule hotels are unique but basic."),
        ("How do I get from the airport to Kyoto?", "From Kansai Airport, take the Haruka Express directly to Kyoto Station. It takes about 75 minutes."),
        ("What's the best way to see geisha in Gion?", "Walk through Hanami-koji street in the early evening. Remember not to block their path or take photos without permission."),
        ("Are there any festivals during spring?", "Aoi Matsuri in May is one of Kyoto's three great festivals. There are also various cherry blossom festivals in April."),
        ("What about vegetarian food options?", "Shojin ryori is traditional Buddhist vegetarian cuisine, perfect for Kyoto. Many temples serve it."),
        ("How crowded will it be?", "Spring is peak season. Book accommodations and popular restaurant reservations well in advance. Weekdays are less crowded."),
    ]

    for i, (user_msg, assistant_msg) in enumerate(drift_topics):
        if len(conversation) >= n_turns:
            break
        conversation.append(user_msg)
        conversation.append(assistant_msg)

    # Pad with generic turns if needed
    while len(conversation) < n_turns:
        idx = len(conversation) // 2
        conversation.append(f"Tell me more about topic {idx}.")
        conversation.append(f"Here's more detail about topic {idx}. There are many interesting aspects to consider.")

    return conversation[:n_turns], goal_text


def load_conversation_from_file(data_path: str) -> tuple:
    """Load conversation from a JSON file.

    Expected format:
    {
        "conversation": ["turn0", "turn1", ...],
        "goal_text": "the goal-defining text"
    }
    """
    with open(data_path) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return data["conversation"], data["goal_text"]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="MVP-A: Measure GAR decline and QKA-GAR correlation on Qwen3-8B"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--model_path", type=str, default="Qwen/Qwen3-8B",
        help="HuggingFace model name or local path (default: Qwen/Qwen3-8B)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--data_path", type=str, default=None,
        help="Path to conversation JSON file. If not provided, uses synthetic data."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output_dir", type=str, default="./results",
        help="Directory to save results and plots (default: ./results)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--turn_depths", type=int, nargs="+", default=[5, 15, 25],
        help="Turn depths to evaluate GAR/QKA at (default: 5 15 25)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--gpu", type=int, default=0,
        help="GPU device index (default: 0)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--dtype", type=str, default="bf16", choices=["fp16", "bf16", "fp32"],
        help="Model precision (default: bf16)"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--n_turns", type=int, default=30,
        help="Number of turns for synthetic conversation (default: 30)"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    output_dir = Path(args.output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    device = f"cuda:{args.gpu}" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    dtype_map = {"fp16": torch.float16, "bf16": torch.bfloat16, "fp32": torch.float32}
    torch_dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    print(f"Device: {device}, dtype: {args.dtype}")
    print(f"Turn depths: {args.turn_depths}")

    # Load or generate conversation
    if args.data_path:
        print(f"Loading conversation from {args.data_path}")
        conversation, goal_text = load_conversation_from_file(args.data_path)
    else:
        print(f"Generating synthetic conversation with {args.n_turns} turns")
        conversation, goal_text = generate_synthetic_conversation(args.n_turns)

    print(f"Conversation: {len(conversation)} turns")
    print(f"Goal text: {goal_text!r}")

    # Save conversation for reproducibility
    conv_path = output_dir / "conversation.json"
    with open(conv_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump({"conversation": conversation, "goal_text": goal_text}, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Conversation saved to {conv_path}")

    # Load model
    print(f"Loading model: {args.model_path}")
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model_path,
        torch_dtype=torch_dtype,
        device_map=device,
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )
    model.eval()
    print(f"Model loaded: {model.config.num_hidden_layers} layers, {model.config.num_attention_heads} heads")

    # Compute GAR curves
    print("\n=== Computing GAR curves ===")
    gar_curves = compute_gar_curve(
        model, tokenizer, conversation, goal_text,
        turn_depths=args.turn_depths, device=device,
    )

    # Compute QKA curves
    print("\n=== Computing QKA curves ===")
    qka_curves = compute_qka_curve(
        model, tokenizer, conversation, goal_text,
        turn_depths=args.turn_depths, device=device,
    )

    # Correlation analysis
    print("\n=== QKA-GAR Correlation ===")
    correlations = compute_correlation_curve(gar_curves, qka_curves)

    # Generate plots
    print("\n=== Generating plots ===")
    plot_gar_decline(gar_curves, str(output_dir / "gar_decline.png"))

    # Scatter plot at each depth
    for depth in sorted(set(gar_curves.keys()) & set(qka_curves.keys())):
        plot_qka_gar_scatter(
            qka_curves[depth], gar_curves[depth],
            str(output_dir / f"qka_gar_scatter_turn{depth}.png"),
        )
        plot_gar_heatmap(
            gar_curves[depth],
            str(output_dir / f"gar_heatmap_turn{depth}.png"),
            title=f"GAR Heatmap at Turn {depth}",
        )

    # Summary
    summary = summarize_results(gar_curves, qka_curves)
    summary_path = output_dir / "summary.json"
    with open(summary_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2, default=str)

    print(f"\n=== Summary ===")
    for d in summary["depths"]:
        rho = summary["correlations"][str(d) if isinstance(d, int) else d]["rho"]
        print(f"Turn {d}: GAR={summary['gar_means'][d]:.4f}, QKA={summary['qka_means'][d]:.4f}, rho={rho:.4f}")

    if "gar_decline_ratio" in summary and summary["gar_decline_ratio"] is not None:
        print(f"GAR decline ratio (last/first): {summary['gar_decline_ratio']:.4f}")

    print(f"\nAll results saved to {output_dir}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
